# **CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._ - All eyes were focused on the gold market at the end of August. Following the sharp price falls seen from the 23rd to the 25th, driven by increases in margins on more than one exchange, the final days of the month provided an opportunity for bargain hunters. With speculation intensifying that the Federal Reserve could yet launch QE3 in the USA, precious metals prices firmed, aided by weak US employment data. Gold recovered most of the ground it had lost and challenged the $1,900 level again, outperforming platinum which is currently trading at a discount to the yellow metal. Silver kept pace with gold in rising above $43. Palladium ignored most of this excitement and continued to gain ground as investors tried to drag it back towards $800. • Unsurprisingly, the most recent commitment of traders report indicates that investors liquidated long COMEX/NYMEX positions in all four of the main precious metals in the week to the 30th of August, amidst collapsing prices for three of them. Japanese investors were somewhat contrarian and were buyers of platinum and gold, providing some muchneeded support for those two metals. • Activity in the precious metal Exchange Traded Funds was muted in the week to the 2nd of September following the previous week’s remarkable price activity. There was some buying in gold but little sign of the fear that has driven the strong inflows of recent weeks. The other three metals all saw some net redemptions by investors with the selling trend now firmly established for palladium. ##### **David Jollie** **david.jollie@mitprecious.com Tel: +44 20 7489 6767** **05 September 2011** ##### **New York:** 200 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10166 0130 Tel: +1 212 878 4122 ##### **London:** 4th Floor, St Martins Court, 10 Paternoster Row, London EC4M 7BB Tel: +44 20 7489 6767 ##### **Hong Kong:** Suite 1306, Two Exchange Square, 8 Connaught Place, Central, Hong Kong Tel: +852 2899 2026 ##### **Tokyo:** 2-1 Ohtemachi 1-Chome, Chiyoda-Ku, Tokyo 100 Tel: +81 33 285 3407 ##### **Singapore:** 80 Robinson Road, #15-02, Singapore, 068898 Tel: +65 6372 8050 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **05 September 2011** ### **Gold CFTC data to 30 August 2011; ETF data to 2 September 2011.** #### **Exchange (COMEX and TOCOM) and ETF Gold Investment (oz)** ||**COMEX**

Following the rapid rise in its price earlier in the month, a sell-off seemed increasingly inevitable and, after gold reached a new all-time high of $1,910 on the 23rd, news of margin increases on COMEX and on the Shanghai Gold Exchange provided the spark to initiate heavy selling. Gold dropped by an incredible $200 to a low of $1,705 on the 25th where an increasing number of investors spied a buying opportunity. Gold bounced back through $1,750 that date and soared to $1,830 on the 29th before the buying slowed. Continued concerns over sovereign debt and a slow global economy were accompanied by growing speculation that QE3 might yet occur. Gold remained the asset of choice and, although the price tested $1,800, few new sellers were found. The price stabilised close to $1,825 at the end of the month before very weak US employment data sent gold sharply higher on the 2nd of September. Gold reached $1,880 that day and has since climbed to test $1,900 again this morning although it has since fallen back to $1,887. #### **Gold Exchange Investment, April 09—August 11** 40 2,000 Gold price, $/oz

- With margins increased on the Shanghai Gold Exchange and on COMEX on the 25th of August, investors were pressed into liquidating some of their long futures positions. Data shows that net long speculative positions fell by 1.5 million ounces during the week to 27.4 million ounces with most of this decline coming from long liquidation. The market now seems well-positioned for another move higher. On TOCOM, Japanese investors were enthusiastic buyers (in contrast to the strong physical selling seen by members of the public) and they added 223,000 ounces to their positions, taking the

m back over one million ounces for the first time since early July. - Following the previous week’s price-driven selling of ETF gold, investors returned to net buying in the week to the 2nd of September. However, despite the rapid run-up in the price, there were no signs of the panic which had been present in recent weeks. 294,000 ounces were added, taking total positions to 67.8 million ounces. 2

- The gold:silver ratio remained almost constant at 44:1 in the final week of August as macroeconomic news drove movements in the prices of both metals. Margin increases on gold drove selling of that metal in China and the USA, with the silver price following gold lower in its fall from $44 on the 23rd of August to $39 on the 25th. Silver seemed oversold at this level and bounced at the same time as gold, shooting as high as $41 later that day before consolidating above that level over the following days as expectations of QE3 slowly started to build. On the 2nd, much worse than expected employment data sent gold soaring and silver followed yet again, leaping from $41

.65 to close the day near to $43.30. It has since weakened marginally and is under pressure close to $42.50. - Open interest in silver declined on COMEX in the week to the 30th of August as the slide in the metal’s price drove long liquidation. Net long speculative positions slipped 18.5 million ounces lower to 268 million ounces. Although this was a substantial decline, it reversed only half of the buying seen in the previous week. The general sense of the market is currently that the silver price is firming and we would expect this to be reflected in additional long exposure by speculators in the next commitment of traders report. - Flows of metal into and out of the silver ETFs were finely balanced in the week to the 2nd of September, with total positions falling by 160,000 ounces to 452.1 million ounces. We feel that the move upwards through $43 on Friday might prompt further buying interest. 3 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **05 September 2011** ### **Platinum CFTC data to 30 August 2011; ETF data to 2 September 2011.** ## **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Platinum Investment (oz)** |**Date**|**Nymex**

- Gold was the main driving force behind the movements in the platinum price in late August. As gold plummeted, platinum fell too, lurching from $1,913 on the 22nd to a low of $1,789 on the 25th. However, during this period, platinum outperformed gold with investors showing a clear preference for the white metal due to

its perceived premium. Once the gold price stabilised and started to move higher again, as speculation over renewed quantitative easing increased, platinum climbed too, reaching $1,820 late on the 25th and surging through $1,850 on the 30th. News that Anglo American Platinum and the South African National Union of Mineworkers had reached agreement over wages emerged on the 31st. Although this was bearish for platinum, the price softened only marginally, falling just below $1,850. The perverse nature of the price movements was illustrated on the 2nd of September. Worse than expected US employment data sent gold rising and, despite the implications of weak industrial demand, platinum followed. It could not quite keep pace with gold, though, and is currently trading at $1,880, with a discount of roughly $12. - Net long speculative interest in platinum on NYMEX fell by 70,000 ounces to 1.64 million ounces in the week to the 30th of August. Non-commercial long futures positions decreased by 8 per cent but short holdings dropped by a quarter, suggesting that the market is looking for further gains in the price of platinum in the weeks ahead. However, positioning remains long, something which threatens the possibility of a sell-off. On TOCOM, the General Public bought a little over a tonne of metal, taking their net long position to 450,000 ounces. - Although the platinum price rebounded from its sub$1,800 lows after the 25th of August, ETF investment was muted. Selling in the Julius Baer fund was the dominant force in driving the sale of 11,000 ounces. Total positions declined to 1.55 million ounces, marginally below their highest ever level. 4 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **05 September 2011** ### **Palladium CFTC data to 303 August 2011; ETF data to 2 September 2011.** ## **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Palladium Investment (oz)** ||**Nymex**

Alone amongst the major precious metals, palladium currently does not seem to be coupled to the gold price. The main target in the near term remains the $800 level, and palladium quietly climbed towards this, rising from $750 on the 25th to almost $780 on the 30th. Investors made an initial attempt on the $800 level on the 2nd of September but the price did not rise far above $790. It has since fallen to just below the $780 level. - Net long speculative positions in palladium on NYMEX fell by 61,000 ounces to 1.36 million ounces in the week to the 30th of August. This was their third decline in the last four weeks, reflecting the increased focus on platinum and the failure of palladium to hold above $800 for an extended period. Open interest fell by 2.0 per cent to 20,360 contracts, a fifth below where they were at the start of August with long liquidation primarily responsible. - The return to net buying in the palladium Exchange Traded Funds in the week to the 26th of August proved to have been a false dawn as selling restarted last week. European selling accounted for most of the decline of 9,500 ounces although there were also some redemptions of precious metal basket shares in the USA. Global holdings now stand at 2.13 million ounces, meaning that ETF investors have supplied 200,000 ounces of palladium to the market this year, the equivalent of the output of a decent-sized mine. 5 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** #### **Disclaimer:** This briefing is for our clients’ information purpose only.
